Differential item functioning by treatment in an intervene_membership() measurement model

intervene_dif.Rd

Tests measurement invariance across treatment groups (the assumption behind the BCH correction of intervene_membership()) with a multigroup latent class model (group = treatment): full invariance against no (or partial) invariance, by the scaled \(\chi^2\) difference test, and reports how \(\Delta_k\) changes when the measurement is allowed to differ between treated and untreated (BCH pseudo-outcomes with treatment-specific classification-error matrices; standard errors treat them as fixed). The print method warns when DIF is significant.

Usage

intervene_dif(
  model,
  data,
  indicators,
  treatment,
  confounders = NULL,
  invariance = "none",
  estimator = c("aipw", "ipw_bch"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  starts = c(100, 20),
  propensity_model = "linear",
  outcome_model = "linear",
  folds = 5,
  trim = 0,
  seed = 20261119,
  learners = NULL,
  bound = 0.01
)

Arguments

model, data, treatment, confounders

As in intervene_membership() (data-frame interface).

indicators

The indicator columns model was fitted to (tidyselect), in order.

invariance

"none" (all items free across groups) or a character vector of the non-invariant items (partial invariance).

estimator

"aipw" (default) or "ipw_bch".

alpha

Test level for the warning.

starts

EM starts of the multigroup models.

propensity_model, outcome_model

Working models for the propensity score (logistic regression) and the latent class regression: "linear" (main effects) or "quadratic" (adds squares, pairwise products and treatment-by-covariate terms). Machine-learning learners are also accepted (see learners).

folds

Number of cross-fitting folds (1 = no cross-fitting).

trim

Truncate estimated propensity scores to [trim, 1 - trim] (0 = no truncation).

seed

Random seed for the fold assignment.

learners

Machine-learning nuisance models. Besides "linear" and "quadratic", propensity_model and outcome_model accept a learner fitted within the cross-fitting training folds: "lasso", "lasso_quadratic", "elasticnet", "ridge" (penalised GLMs with cross-validated \(\lambda\)), "forest" (random forest), "boost" (gradient-boosted trees; needs the Julia package EvoTrees.jl) or "superlearner" (stacked ensemble). With a learner, the class regression estimates \(P(\hat c = j \mid A = a, X)\) in each arm and maps it through \(D^{-1}\). learners is the library of the "superlearner": a character vector of names ("mean", "glm", "glm_quadratic", "lasso", "lasso_quadratic", "elasticnet", "ridge", "forest", "boost"), or NULL for the default library (mean, glm, lasso, lasso_quadratic, forest).

bound

With a learner, propensity scores are bounded to [bound, 1 - bound] (forests can predict 0 or 1). Not applied to "linear" / "quadratic".

Value

An object of class lcc_dif_result with chisq, df, p, scaled, delta_invariant, se_invariant, delta_noninvariant, se_noninvariant, change, significant.

How to use

  1. Pass the measurement model of intervene_membership(), the data frame it was fitted to and its indicators (same columns, same order), with the treatment and confounders.

  2. Run it with all items free across treatment groups (invariance = "none") or with a vector of item names for partial invariance.

  3. Read the scaled \(\chi^2\) difference test first: if it does not reject, report it and keep the invariant \(\Delta_k\) (the change is then noise).

  4. If it rejects, check that the classes keep their meaning in both groups, then compare the invariant and non-invariant \(\Delta_k\). See vignette("function-guide").

See also

intervene_membership(), intervene_membership_sensitivity()

Examples

# \donttest{
data(programme)
# Question: do the wellbeing items measure the classes in the same way for participants
# and non-participants (the assumption behind the BCH correction)?
m <- latentmixtures::lca(programme, low_mood:friends, K = 3)
#> Starting Julia ...
d <- intervene_dif(m, programme, indicators = low_mood:friends, treatment = programme,
                   confounders = c(female, age, low_ses, distress, belonging))
d
#> ▸ Differential item functioning by treatment (programme)
#>   Scaled chi-square difference test, full vs non-invariant measurement: chi2(24) = 22.79, p = .532
#> 
#>   ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>            Delta (invariant)     SE  Delta (non-inv.)     SE  change
#>   ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   Class 1              0.194  0.031             0.132  0.032  −0.062
#>   Class 2             −0.052  0.037            −0.021  0.037   0.030
#>   Class 3             −0.143  0.021            −0.111  0.023   0.032
#>   ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#>   No significant DIF: the change column is noise around zero.
# chi2(24) = 22.79, p = .532: no evidence of DIF, so report the invariant estimates
# (0.196, -0.055, -0.141); the change column (e.g. -0.062) is then noise.
# }
